epithet.en: A noblewoman shipwrecked on the coast of Illyria, disguised as the page Cesario

2.modern-en: Viola lands on the Illyrian coast, hears that her brother Sebastian may have drowned, and decides to disguise herself as a young man and enter Duke Orsino's service.

4.modern-en: Viola, now 'Cesario,' is sent by Orsino to woo Countess Olivia on his behalf, and confides in an aside that she would rather marry him herself.

5.modern-en: Viola arrives at Olivia's house and refuses to leave until she is admitted; she delivers Orsino's love speech and watches Olivia fall for her instead.

7.modern-en: Viola is overtaken by Malvolio with the ring Olivia has pretended she left behind, and works out that the countess has fallen for her.

9.modern-en: Viola listens to Orsino's discourse on love and quietly tells him, in coded language, the story of a sister who never declared her own.

11.modern-en: Viola returns to Olivia's garden and is given Olivia's open declaration of love, which she cannot accept.

14.modern-en: Viola is forced into a duel with Sir Andrew by Sir Toby's mischief and is saved by the intervention of Antonio.

16.modern-en: Viola is mentioned offstage as Sebastian's enemies and friends mistake the twins for each other.

18.modern-en: Viola meets Sebastian face-to-face at last, is recognised by him and by Orsino, and accepts the Duke's offer of marriage.

1.modern-en: Orsino opens the play with 'If music be the food of love' and complains that Olivia has shut herself away in mourning.

4.modern-en: Orsino takes 'Cesario' into his confidence and sends him to plead his love to Olivia.

9.modern-en: Orsino calls for music and discourses on love and women with Cesario, telling him that no woman's love can equal his.

18.modern-en: Orsino confronts Olivia in the street, witnesses the unmasking of the twins, and turns at the end to Viola with an offer of marriage.

epithet.en: A wealthy Illyrian countess in mourning for her brother

5.modern-en: Olivia receives Cesario in her house, lets the Duke's messenger lift her veil, and finds herself charmed.

8.modern-en: Olivia is woken at night by Sir Toby's drunken party and complains of his disorder.

11.modern-en: Olivia receives Cesario again in the garden and confesses her love to him outright.

12.modern-en: Olivia is alarmed by Malvolio's smiling, cross-gartered behaviour and concludes he must be mad.

14.modern-en: Olivia meets Sebastian by chance in the street, takes him for Cesario, and rushes him into a betrothal in front of a priest.

17.modern-en: Olivia formally exchanges contracts with Sebastian in her chapel, still believing him to be Cesario.

18.modern-en: Olivia is at the centre of the final unmasking; she discovers she has married Sebastian and is reconciled with the truth.

5.modern-en: Malvolio reproves Olivia for taking pleasure in the fool's jests and is told he is sick of self-love.

8.modern-en: Malvolio interrupts Sir Toby's late-night carouse with threats of being put out, and is mocked for his pains.

10.modern-en: Malvolio finds the forged letter in the box-tree, reads it aloud, and resolves to appear smiling, cross-gartered, and in yellow stockings.

12.modern-en: Malvolio appears before Olivia in the prescribed costume, quoting the letter; she concludes he has lost his mind and orders him cared for.

16.modern-en: Malvolio is locked in a dark room and visited by Feste impersonating the curate Sir Topas, who 'examines' him.

18.modern-en: Malvolio is brought out at last, given his forged letter back, learns that he has been the victim of a trick, and storms off vowing revenge on the whole pack of them.

3.modern-en: Sir Toby introduces Sir Andrew Aguecheek to Maria as a suitor for Olivia and persuades him to stay on in Illyria.

5.modern-en: Sir Toby blunders in drunk while Olivia is receiving Cesario and is dismissed by his niece.

8.modern-en: Sir Toby leads the late-night drinking that brings Malvolio to scold the household, and proposes the revenge plot against him.

10.modern-en: Sir Toby hides in the box-tree to watch Malvolio find Maria's forged letter.

11.modern-en: Sir Toby goads Sir Andrew into challenging Cesario to a duel.

14.modern-en: Sir Toby stages the duel between Cesario and Sir Andrew and is mistakenly attacked by Sebastian.

17.modern-en: Sir Toby is bandaged up after his beating by Sebastian and admits he is sick of the whole business.

18.modern-en: Sir Toby is reported, in the closing scene, to have married Maria for her invention of the Malvolio trick.

epithet.en: Sir Toby's foolish friend, hopeful suitor of Olivia

3.modern-en: Sir Andrew is presented to Maria, fumbles the introduction, and is persuaded by Sir Toby to stay on as a suitor.

8.modern-en: Sir Andrew joins the late-night singing party and helps provoke Malvolio's intervention.

10.modern-en: Sir Andrew is in the box-tree as Malvolio reads the forged letter.

14.modern-en: Sir Andrew is pushed by Sir Toby into a duel with Cesario, retreats from it, and is then drubbed by Sebastian.

18.modern-en: Sir Andrew limps onstage in the final scene with bloodied head, having been beaten by Sebastian thinking he was Cesario.

3.modern-en: Maria scolds Sir Toby for his drinking and trades wit with Sir Andrew on his first appearance.

5.modern-en: Maria announces Cesario at Olivia's gate.

8.modern-en: Maria proposes the revenge plot against Malvolio: she will forge a letter in Olivia's hand.

10.modern-en: Maria plants the letter in the garden where Malvolio will find it and watches him fall for it.

12.modern-en: Maria reports Malvolio's smiling cross-gartered approach to Olivia.

17.modern-en: Maria is named in the late preparations for the masque-prank in the dark room.

18.modern-en: Maria is reported, at the close, to have married Sir Toby in reward for her invention.

5.modern-en: Feste appears before Olivia for the first time, gets back into her good graces by proving her a fool, and offends Malvolio in the process.

8.modern-en: Feste joins Sir Toby and Sir Andrew in the late-night singing and earns his sixpences for catches and ballads.

9.modern-en: Feste sings 'Come away, come away, death' for Orsino in the Duke's chamber.

11.modern-en: Feste meets Cesario in the garden and pronounces wisdom in his own coin.

16.modern-en: Feste impersonates the curate Sir Topas to torment the imprisoned Malvolio in the dark room.

18.modern-en: Feste closes the play alone on stage, singing 'When that I was and a little tiny boy' as the rain refrain falls.

6.modern-en: Sebastian, rescued from the wreck by Antonio, decides to go on to Orsino's court alone.

13.modern-en: Sebastian and Antonio arrive in Illyria; Sebastian goes off to see the sights while Antonio waits at their inn.

15.modern-en: Sebastian is set upon in the street by Sir Andrew and Sir Toby, who think he is Cesario, and easily beats them both.

17.modern-en: Sebastian meets Olivia in the garden, is rushed into a betrothal he does not understand, and quietly accepts his luck.

18.modern-en: Sebastian arrives in the final scene, recognises Viola, and is recognised by Olivia as the man she has actually married.

6.modern-en: Antonio takes leave of Sebastian on the coast, then resolves to follow him to Orsino's court despite his enmity with the Duke.

13.modern-en: Antonio gives Sebastian his purse for any incidental expenses and waits for him at the Elephant inn.

15.modern-en: Antonio breaks up Cesario's duel with Sir Andrew, mistaking him for Sebastian, and is arrested by Orsino's officers.

18.modern-en: Antonio is brought before Orsino in the closing scene and is bewildered to see two Sebastians.
